newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 a tonne weaker on Tuesday, amid selling prompted by reports of a sizeable mid-crop in Ivory Coast, traders said.

Output at the world's biggest producer is shaping up for a 1996/97 cocoa midcrop of at least 150,000 tonnes, but young pod survival into mid-May will determine final estimates, crop analysts and exporters said.

Meantime, Ivory Coast's semi-finished cocoa product and powder exports were steady in February compared with month-ago figures, but up from the same year-ago period. The increase was attributed to new processing factory capacity.
Monday, CSCE July settled $23 weaker at $1,440 a tonne, traded $1,446 to $1,427. Volume was light at an estimated 4,610 lots.
Support was pegged at $1,400 per tonne in the July contract.

LIFFE cocoa futures eased across the board Tuesday, with switches and against actuals (AAs) dominating trade. May stood seven stg lower at 996 stg per tonne, and July down seven to 1,014 stg at the midday break.
